<p class="nv-section-lead">The reason Novis exists. Isolation, capabilities, and two compile-time qualifiers that keep untrusted data and secrets out of the places where they do damage. Every rule here holds while the language is running; what an editor conceals on a screen is the editor's chapter, not this one.</p>

<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/security/isolates/">Isolates</a><span class="nv-section-count">8</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Running another script shares nothing but compiled code. Values cross by copy, failure crosses as data, and the budget is the tree.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/isolates/#isolate-shares-nothing">Running another script is an in-process isolate that shares nothing with its parent but compiled code</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/isolates/#isolate-values-cross-by-copy">A value crosses an isolate boundary as one graph copy, and a closure, an alias or a host handle does not cross at all</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/isolates/#isolate-budget-is-the-trees">A request and everything it spawns share one budget, accounted at the tree's root</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/isolates/#isolate-failure-is-a-value">A child isolate's failure arrives as data on the result and never unwinds into its parent</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/isolates/#isolate-output-is-captured">An isolate's output is captured by default and carries the parent's sink carrier</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/isolates/#isolate-teardown-is-a-drain-then-a-sweep">An isolate ends by draining implementation</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>

<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/">The closed doors</a><span class="nv-section-count">9</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">No FFI, no <code>eval</code>, no scheme-dispatching path, no cross-request state. Four doors closed by construction, reopened by nothing.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#script-spawn-capability">Executing code is its own capability, and the entry path is canonicalised and then prefix-checked</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#request-state-throws-in-an-isolate">Request, server and session state throws where there is no inbound request, rather than answering empty</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#no-cross-request-state">Nothing a request does is observable by another request except through an explicit, capability-gated store</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#closed-doors">Four doors are closed by construction, and no configuration reopens any of them</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#no-ffi">No userland mechanism loads native code into the process</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#no-eval">There is no <code>eval</code>, and no <code>Core</code> member compiles a string produced at run time</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#a-path-is-not-a-url">A path is a filesystem path: no member dispatches on a scheme prefix, and nothing may register one</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#reflection-enforces-visibility">A reflective call faces exactly the visibility check ordinary code at that site would, and there is no <code>setAccessible</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#reflection-needs-no-capability">Reflection and AST parsing are capability-free, because neither reaches the world outside the process</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/security/capabilities/">Capabilities and authority</a><span class="nv-section-count">8</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">The check lives inside the function that performs the effect, and authority belongs to the namespace enclosing the code.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/capabilities/#capability-check-at-the-door">The capability check lives inside the function that performs the effect, and that door is the only way out of the process</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/capabilities/#capability-question-is-grant-and-scope">A capability question is a grant and a scope, asked of the request's own configuration snapshot</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/capabilities/#capability-declaration-is-one-table">What each <code>Core</code> member needs is declared once in one table, and nothing at run time reads it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/capabilities/#capability-roster-is-closed">Every capability name that exists is on one roster, and a name outside it is refused where it is written</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/capabilities/#authority-is-the-enclosing-namespace">Authority is a property of the namespace enclosing the code, never of the nesting depth or the name being called</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/capabilities/#grants-are-keyed-on-a-namespace">The application's grant table is keyed on namespace prefixes, and a capability it names must be on the roster</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/capabilities/#longest-prefix-wins">The longest matching grant key wins, and a subtree is spelled out because it reaches code that does not exist yet</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/capabilities/#an-unmatched-namespace-holds-the-application">A namespace matching no grant line holds the application's own authority, and a fetch leaves nothing unmatched</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/">Scopes, denial and the address policy</a><span class="nv-section-count">10</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">How a path scope is decided, why a denial is catchable, and why the network address policy lives inside the capability itself.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#path-scope-canonicalise-then-prefix">A path scope is canonicalise-then-prefix over whole components, and a path that does not exist yet is its deepest existing ancestor</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#denial-is-a-runtime-error">A denied capability is a catchable <code>RuntimeError</code> naming the capability, never a fatal</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#optional-capability-degrades">A capability is required or optional, and only a required one refuses to build</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#no-runtime-grant">Two layers enforce a capability and only the static one grants; nothing anywhere widens</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#capability-costs-nothing-unasked">A member that needs no capability pays nothing, and one that does pays only beside a syscall</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#package-authority-is-granted-one-line-at-a-time">A dependency's authority is granted by the application one line at a time, and a declaration grants nothing</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#process-exec-capability">Executing a program is deny-by-default under its own capability, and there is no shell to interpolate into</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#net-address-policy"><code>net.connect</code> carries an address policy that denies the private ranges, and an exception is one written IP address</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#net-listen-is-a-separate-grant-from-net-connect">The grant follows what the program is doing rather than the transport: reaching out is <code>net.connect</code>, binding is <code>net.listen</code>, and neither widens the other</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/scopes-and-denial/#the-policy-lives-in-the-capability">The address policy lives in the capability, so every client obeys it and none of them may hold its own</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/">Tainted data and its sinks</a><span class="nv-section-count">10</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Everything from outside arrives <code>tainted</code>, it poisons what it touches, and a sink is any parameter a parser will execute.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#tainted-qualifier"><code>tainted</code> is a compile-time qualifier on <code>string</code>, <code>bytes</code> and a shape of them, spellable in any declaration and erased before codegen</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#tainted-sources">Every accessor that hands a program bytes from outside answers the <code>tainted</code> form, and the list of them is enumerable</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#taint-propagation">A tainted operand poisons every operation it takes part in, and only a checked conversion launders for free</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#sink-predicate">A <code>string</code> or <code>bytes</code> parameter is a sink when its content becomes an instruction a parser executes</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#unclassified-parameter-refuses-tainted">A <code>Core</code> parameter nobody classified refuses a tainted argument, and refuses to ship at all</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#every-grammar-is-a-sink">Every grammar the library parses is a sink, and none of the four gets a launderer</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#regex-pattern-is-a-sink">A regex pattern is a sink with no launderer; the subject is data and may be tainted</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#outbound-url-is-a-sink">An outbound URL or address is a sink, and a tainted one is refused where it is written</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#metric-label-refuses-tainted">A metric label value refuses <code>tainted</code>, and there is deliberately no launderer for one</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#log-is-not-a-sink">A log field is data, so it takes a tainted value and wants one</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/security/laundering/">Laundering</a><span class="nv-section-count">8</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">The only ways out of <code>tainted</code>: a member named for the one sink it is safe for, a typed capture, or a written assertion.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/laundering/#launderers-are-sink-named">The only way out of <code>tainted</code> is a <code>Core</code> member whose contract names the one sink it is safe for</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/laundering/#launderer-answers-a-carrier">A launderer answers its sink's carrier when that sink launders on its own and the transform is not idempotent, and a plain type otherwise</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/laundering/#capture-answers-the-carrier">Capturing a sink yields that sink's carrier, never a plain <code>string</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/laundering/#route-capture-is-laundered-by-its-type">A route capture is laundered by the parameter's own type, and a <code>string</code> capture stays tainted</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/laundering/#derived-codec-qualifiers">A derived codec adds no qualifier rule, and a <code>secret</code> field is refused at the declaration rather than silently omitted</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/laundering/#assert-trusted"><code>Core\Taint::assertTrusted</code> is the one generic way out, and it carries a written reason at the call site</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/laundering/#response-body-is-one-typed-member">A response body is written by one typed member, and mixing <code>echo</code> with one of them does not compile</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/laundering/#db-pool-reset-is-a-boundary">A pooled database connection is proven clean before it is reused, and a failed reset destroys it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/security/secrets/">Secrets</a><span class="nv-section-count">8</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">A second, independent qualifier. Every sink refuses it, it crosses no boundary, comparing two is constant-time, and no rendering the toolchain prints carries one in the clear.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/secrets/#secret-qualifier"><code>secret</code> is a second, independent compile-time qualifier, written before <code>tainted</code> and in that order alone</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/secrets/#secret-has-no-ambient-source">Nothing grants <code>secret</code> ambiently; it appears where a developer wrote it, and at one member that is its own contract</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/secrets/#secret-propagation">A <code>secret</code> operand poisons its own axis independently of <code>tainted</code>, and a checked conversion strips it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/secrets/#secret-sinks-refuse">Every output sink refuses a <code>secret</code> value outright, and no auto-escape or neutralisation bypasses one</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/secrets/#secret-crosses-no-boundary">A <code>secret</code> value is refused at the one graph copy, so it reaches neither <code>serialize</code> nor any spawn</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/secrets/#secret-comparison-is-constant-time">Comparing two <code>secret</code> values with <code>==</code> lowers to a constant-time helper, decided by the compiler</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/secrets/#secret-in-a-test-report">A <code>secret</code> operand is compared but never rendered, and no flag lifts the redaction</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/secrets/#redaction-reaches-the-tools-own-renderings">No rendering the toolchain itself produces prints a <code>secret</code> in the clear, the AST dump included</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/security/extensions-and-qualifiers/">Qualifiers across an extension</a><span class="nv-section-count">7</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">An extension manifest may only tighten. Contagion is the default, and no spelling anywhere removes a qualifier.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/extensions-and-qualifiers/#extension-manifest-only-tightens">Everything an extension manifest may declare is a restriction, so a hostile manifest cannot make a calling program less safe</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/extensions-and-qualifiers/#extension-grants-are-an-intersection">An extension's files and outbound HTTP are the intersection of its entry's grant, its manifest's request and its caller's own grant</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/extensions-and-qualifiers/#extension-contagion">An extension call is an ordinary operation for taint, so contagion is the default and needs no declaration</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/extensions-and-qualifiers/#extension-declares-sink-or-source">An extension manifest may declare exactly two things: a parameter that refuses <code>tainted</code>, and a return that is always <code>tainted</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/extensions-and-qualifiers/#extension-cannot-launder">No extension may remove the <code>tainted</code> qualifier, in any manifest spelling</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/extensions-and-qualifiers/#secret-does-not-cross-an-extension">A <code>secret</code> value is refused at every extension boundary, in either direction</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/extensions-and-qualifiers/#image-component-declares-nothing">The image component declares no qualifier deviation and requests no capability</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/security/protocols-and-tokens/">Protocols, tokens and CSRF</a><span class="nv-section-count">12</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">One TLS client, a closed protocol roster, an algorithm that comes from the key, and CSRF on by default.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/protocols-and-tokens/#one-tls-client">There is one TLS client in the tree, and a driver reaches it over a generic transport rather than PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/protocols-and-tokens/#protocol-roster">A closed roster of application-layer security protocols lives in <code>Core</code>, and nothing joins it without meeting the test</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/protocols-and-tokens/#protocol-admission-test">Three conditions without an expiry, or past one, fails verification, and no flag disables the check</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a <code>A256GCM</code> alone, and the static that built the key picks the algorithm</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/protocols-and-tokens/#jws-issued-subset">A token another party issued verifies against a key found by <code>kid</code>, never one that is tried, and its claims come back as a <code>tainted</code> shape</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/protocols-and-tokens/#csrf-is-on-by-default">The server refuses an unsafe verb without a valid CSRF token, and the opt-out is written on the route itself</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/protocols-and-tokens/#access-is-checked-for-presence-not-meaning">The compiler proves a route's access decision was written, never that it was honoured</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/security/bidi-and-passwords/">Bidirectional text and password hashes</a><span class="nv-section-count">9</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">A two-counter predicate against direction-flipping source, and a hash surface that writes one algorithm and reads exactly two.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/bidi-and-passwords/#bidi-predicate">A span is rejected when it ends with a directional scope still open, decided by two counters</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/bidi-and-passwords/#bidi-boundaries">The lexer refuses an unterminated control and the sinks substitute it, and nobody writes a second predicate</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/bidi-and-passwords/#bidi-scope-is-the-whole-target">Zero-width characters, homoglyphs and the full bidirectional algorithm are deliberately outside the check</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/bidi-and-passwords/#hash-writes-argon2id-only"><code>hash</code> writes Argon2id and nothing else, and no member takes an algorithm argument</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/bidi-and-passwords/#bcrypt-read-roster">A stored password hash is read from a roster of exactly two shapes, and the roster grows only by amendment</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/bidi-and-passwords/#needs-rehash-answers-weaker"><code>needsRehash</code> measures weaker rather than different, so every bcrypt hash asks to be rewritten</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/bidi-and-passwords/#bcrypt-cost-ceiling">A stored bcrypt cost above 17 is refused before any work is done</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/bidi-and-passwords/#bcrypt-truncation">bcrypt's 72-byte truncation is replicated exactly, because the stored row was written under it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/security/bidi-and-passwords/#an-unreadable-stored-hash-throws">A stored value outside the read roster throws, and the message never quotes the bytes</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
